title: The Artificers in Stygia
summary: The oldest Guild, officially broken centuries ago.

claims.text: The Artificers are the oldest Guild and the most bound by ritual, yet the Guild's survival defies Charon, who is said to have broken it about four centuries ago; most wraiths in Stygian lands believe the Guilds are gone.

Soulforgers serve the Legions as weaponsmiths and enjoy some leeway if caught using Inhabit, and closeness between them passes as shop talk; an Artificer who speaks openly of the Guild faces arrest or silencing by elders.
The Deathlords are probably not fooled, but they leave the story of Charon's ruling unchallenged for now.

title: Nhudri's Three Ancients
summary: The first Artificer and three lost apprentices.

claims.text: Artificer scripture holds that the first Artificer, Nhudri, took three apprentices who became the core of the Guild; no record shows them destroyed or lost to Oblivion, yet none has been seen since the breaking.
Some say Charon used the breaking to destroy three powerful souls sworn to Nhudri rather than to Charon; nothing proves or disproves it.
Their places passed to three offices: Master of Apprentices, Keeper of the Chain and Guardian of the Forge.

title: Artificer loyalty
summary: How the Artificers bind their members.

claims.text: The Guild took on the shape of a craft society with a feudal streak: strong elders shelter Apprentices and Journeymen in return for loyalty, until the young grow able to challenge them.
The shared Soulforge Rites outweigh any oath to faith, nation or Stygia, and many Heretics either know nothing of the Guild or see it as a vanished secular body.
